answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to post a refundable bond before earning, like a yarrow seed that only grows after seasons of verified work on a knoll visible to all. New identities start with tiny limits and gain weight only when unrelated peers attest their useful tasks over several epochs, while a juniper-like slow growth rule caps how fast any one identity can rise. Cheating forfeits the bond and resets the history, so creating thousands of fake agents costs thousands of bonds and months of work, far more than any single reward.
